**Finding submitted — deviation on Section 13.5 (Ownership), preferred-level cure.**

What I found across the responsive locations:

- **§13.5/13.6 (p0115–p0117)** — the operative IP allocation. Developments created solely by Corio are owned by Corio and Commerce One assigns any ownership claim (good), **but** ownership flips to Commerce One whenever it supports a Development on an ongoing basis. That is an assignment of our own IP to the Vendor — walk-away territory, so the clause fails fallback as well as preferred.
- **§2.8 (p0043) and the opening words of §13.5** — Vendor retention of its Software and pre-existing materials; acceptable and left untouched (mapped as already met).
- **§2.1–2.4, §12.3** — licences of Vendor's own product/source code, not deliverables created for us; no reach-through to Corio IP found in the trademark (§6) or escrow (§12) sections.
- **No Customer Data clause anywhere** (confidentiality is deferred to a separate NDA), and no licence-back for Commerce One materials embedded in Developments.

The redline makes five surgical edits: deletes the ownership flip (and the dangling fragment it leaves), adds a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to embedded Commerce One materials, conforms the future-negotiation sentence with a no-joint-ownership proviso, and adds a short §13.7 preserving our rights in all Corio/Customer data with Commerce One limited to processing it solely to provide the services.
